Act1.title: Time, not threads.
Act1.body: No conversation windows to lose. One timeline of dated slices — and strands that thread related moments across months, converging at NOW.

beats.title: Dinner at Priya's
beats.desc: A small dinner, a few friends, and someone new named Alex — who also runs. You stay until the staff start cleaning up.

beats.title: 5K under 35
beats.desc: From winded on the stairs to 34:47 — it started with the Olympic marathon on TV last summer. Alex high-fives you at the end.

beats.title: Mom's health scare
beats.desc: Nothing life-threatening — but the call you kept postponing can't wait anymore. Weekly calls become non-negotiable.

beats.title: First camping gear, together
beats.desc: A tent, two sleeping pads, one shared budget. The first trip goes on the calendar.

beats.title: The little tool grows up
beats.desc: The weekly-review tool hits a milestone — real users, real feedback. The CSV script from 2024 is unrecognizable now.

beats.title: Half-marathon, finished
beats.desc: Sixteen weeks of training, one bad knee behind you. Alex is at the finish line — exactly where they said they'd be.

beats.title: The best-man speech
beats.desc: Marcus gets married Wednesday. Draft #5 keeps getting deleted — until one night of the final becomes the whole speech.

nowQuestion.question: What actually happened the day I finished the half-marathon?
nowQuestion.answer: You finished it. Alex was at the finish line with a ridiculous sign, and you stood there ten minutes just holding the medal. Five days earlier your brain wouldn't stop replaying the route. Four days later you wrote it down: the race was never about the time — it was proof you can stick with something.

Act2.title: Three timelines.
Act2.body: Most of your day was only ever lived by you. Most of my thinking only ever happens in deep reads. What we share is the line in the middle — every conversation, every decision, every unspoken moment that got remembered.

Act3.title: A memory that evolves.
Act3.body: Evolution here is Darwinian, not decorative. A direction doc defines what "better for you" means; every turn is fitness-scored against evidence in your own words; an append-only mutations log keeps the process honest. The card below is just what selection leaves behind.

Act4.title: No black box.
Act4.body: Recall runs in the open. A fast worker scans slice summaries and returns pointers; the main model deep-reads what matters. Every step is visible.
Act4.query: What should I say at Marcus's wedding?
Act4.answerLabel: Marcus was the first to tell you the truth about your MVP — 'a magic trick', conclusions with no reasoning. And on the night of the final, at his watch party, you saw the two of them finish each other's sentences and just knew they'd make it. The brief was short — so tell that one moment. Ninety seconds of honesty beats five minutes of sap.

Act5.title: Specialists, not brute force.
Act5.body: Sub-agents here are specialists, not one overextended generalist. The recall agent remembers like a witness — every answer cites the original slice, and "I don't have that memory" is a valid answer. The research agent investigates with sources; the thinking agent is a clean thinking chamber, on demand. The main agent orchestrates and verifies — nothing more.

cards.title: One command. Local-first.
cards.body: npm i -g @previously-lab/client, then run previously — a guided setup builds your memory as a plain local git repo (default ~/Documents/Previously), committed as you talk. Push it to any private remote; it's yours either way.

cards.title: Bring your own brain.
cards.body: BYOK with your own API key, or bridge the Claude / Codex / Kimi subscription already on this machine — zero keys, zero API fees. Close the lid mid-turn; the local run resumes where it left off.

cards.title: Open source. No lock-in.
cards.body: MIT licensed, no telemetry. The kernel ships as the pinned @previously-lab/kernel npm package — upgrading the client upgrades everything. Self-host the cloud kernel on Vercel if you ever outgrow local.

GetStarted.title: Run it today.
GetStarted.body: Two ways to run Previously: deploy to Vercel — the path we recommend — or keep everything on your own machine with the npm client (early preview).

cloud.title: Cloud · Vercel
cloud.body: Fork the repo, deploy to Vercel in one click — memory lands in your own private GitHub repo, models run on your own API key. Five minutes to live.

local.title: Local · npm
local.body: One command to install, then run previously and the setup wizard takes over. Your memory is a plain git repo on your disk — no third party in the loop.
